A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Zoomer framework and provide readable text, figures, tables and algorithms. The v1 appendix was inspected; its NMS algorithm and example figures are incorporated into v2's main text rather than removed.

before.justification: v1 reports original pilot experiments, benchmark evaluations, token and latency measurements, and component ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds open-source model evaluations, additional baseline comparisons, a threshold study and a failure case.

M1.justification: The three modules, four Zoomer variants and both algorithms are retained. However, v2 Section 4.2 newly states that every configuration supplies exactly one reconstructed image, while Table 2 and Section 5.3 retain v1's description of separately supplied patches. This conflict prevents determining whether input construction actually changed. Newly documented parsing, scaling and threshold details alone do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VSTAR, CVBench-2D/3D, RealWorldQA, ScienceQA, MMVP, MMMU, HR-4K/8K and TerraIncognita. The added experiments reuse existing benchmark coverage; additional model backbones and a validation-set threshold study change settings rather than datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons against V* in Table 7 and Random-Patches and Uniform-Patches in Table 8. Table 6 also compares Qwen2-VL-7B and InternVL2.5-8B with and without Zoomer. These substantially expand the comparisons beyond v1's input-processing baselines and component variants.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include two specified open-source backbones, equal-patch-count controls, and a VSTAR validation study sweeping thresholds 0.25, 0.35 and 0.45. The existing commercial-model decoding settings and TerraIncognita zero-shot/15-shot design remain unchanged. These are added protocols, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The detector, emphasis-method and prompting ablations in Table 5 are retained. v2 additionally tests semantic patch selection under a matched patch budget, sensitivity to the adaptive global-view threshold, and failure when the detector misses a question-critical small object. These add substantive controlled, sensitivity and failure analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions give only qualitative repeated-evaluation statements in Section 5.3: multiple measurements in v1 and multiple trials in v2. Neither provides run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests, and no new statistical estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 are unchanged, but Tables 6–9 add substantial results. For example, Table 6 reports VSTAR accuracy of 0.573 without Zoomer and 0.655 with Zoomer for InternVL2.5-8B. v2 also adds the detector-failure finding and corrects the pilot prose from 0.76 to 64% Zoomed Crop accuracy, matching the unchanged Table 1.

T1.justification: Equation 1 adds an explicit mathematical definition of cropped-region area relative to original-image area and specifies the 0.35 decision inequality; v1 described the threshold informally. Both algorithms remain unchanged, and no theorem, proof or formal guarantee is added. The standard relative-token-saving formula is explanatory rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central framework and accuracy/efficiency claims remain. v2's introduction adds a priority claim of the first in-depth empirical analysis and incorrectly calls the VSTAR improvement a 26.9% absolute gain. Both versions' Table 2 supports an increase from 56.5% to 71.7%: 15.2 percentage points, or approximately 26.9% relative.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the limitations and interpretation beyond v1's patch-fragmentation discussion. It explains why missed detections can defeat even the adaptive global view, explicitly acknowledges that the pipeline is heuristic, and discusses detector-free alternatives and future explicit optimization. It also adds causal interpretations of the fixed-budget controls and threshold study, although some conflict with the method description.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents automatic inference-time RoIs without ground-truth boxes, dependency-parser priority ordering, per-RoI 512-pixel normalization with a native-resolution cap, validation-based selection of the 0.35 threshold, and provider-token versus patch-proxy accounting. These substantially expand operational disclosure; they do not establish that all underlying procedures changed, and the single-canvas description remains inconsistent.

R1.justification: The related-work sections and bibliography largely retain the same works. v2 extends positioning through its new first-analysis claim, direct comparison with the previously cited V*, and discussion of applicability to open-source and high-resolution models. This is a limited positioning extension rather than a substantial literature expansion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, pilot discussion, results, ablation discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The title changes to Adaptive Visual Token Allocation, results gain research-question subheadings, and the appendix material is integrated into the main narrative. These are substantial editorial and structural changes.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column journal layout, substantially resizing and redistributing tables and algorithms. Figures 4–5 and Algorithm 2 move from the appendix into the main text. Four new tables and the failure-case Figure 6 are added; Figures 1–5 otherwise retain their content.

improvement.justification: The new stronger-baseline comparisons, fixed-budget controls, open-source results and detector-failure analysis provide useful evidence missing from v1, and the pilot prose now matches Table 1. However, v2 introduces conflicting single-image versus separate-patch descriptions, reverses the stated threshold rule in its interpretation, and mislabels a relative gain as absolute. These inconsistencies limit the net improvement despite the expanded evidence.
